events.text:
Control flow for `priceShoppingCart` (`ShoppingCartService.java:54-87`), from the CFG (`inspect priceShoppingCart cfg`):

- **Guard branch** (line 56): `if (sc != null)`. False routes straight to exit (block_1 → block_0), skipping everything; true continues at line 58 via `initShoppingCartForPricing(sc)`.
- **Compound branch** (line 60): `list != null && list.size() > 0` is lowered as two blocks (block_3, block_4) with short-circuit edges — either false jumps to line 81. True runs line 62 `ps.applyCartItemPromotions(sc)`.
- **Loop** (line 64): for-each over `sc.getShoppingCartItemList()` is block_6 with `iftrue` into body block_7 and `iffalse` to block_8; body (lines 66-68) accumulates `cartItemPromoSavings` and `cartItemTotal`, then a `jump` back edge to block_6.
- **Threshold branch** (line 74): after loop, line 72 sets shipping total; `if (cartItemTotal >= 25)` runs insurance at line 75 (`iftrue`), else falls to line 81 (`iffalse`).
- **Merge/exit** (lines 81-83): `applyShippingPromotions` and `setCartTotal`, then exit.

Note the loop body is reached only when the cart is non-empty; the final merge at line 81 is reachable from all inner branches.

events.text: At line 68, which statements contribute to `sc`, and why?

input.description: Slice at line 68 for variable sc

caption.title: Program dependence, not line matching
caption.body: Only statements that influence the value or carry untrusted data are included.

events.name: Read

events.text:
The backward slice at line 68 for `sc` (`slice … --line 68 --variable sc --function priceShoppingCart`) keeps two statements, reducing the file by 83.3%:

- Line 66 `sc.setCartItemPromoSavings(sc.getCartItemPromoSavings() + sci.getPromoSavings() * sci.getQuantity())` — reaches line 68 via a `data` edge on `sc` (also `sci` and `getQuantity`).
- Line 68 itself (the criterion).

Why line 66: it is the only prior intra-procedural statement that mutates the same `sc` object within the loop body; line 68 reads accumulated `sc.getCartItemTotal()`, so the PDG links the aliased `sc` state from 66 into 68.

Two contributors are *not* in the slice and are worth flagging:
- Line 58 `initShoppingCartForPricing(sc)` initializes `cartItemTotal`/prices (`ShoppingCartService.java:91`, `:102`); this is an interprocedural side effect the slice doesn't model.
- Line 68's own earlier loop iterations (loop-carried dependence, back-edge block_7 → block_6) — the CFG shows the back edge but no self data edge was emitted.

Loop header/condition reads (line 60, 64) supply `sc`/`sci` but aren't mutation contributors.

events.text:
Dominator tree from `inspect priceShoppingCart dom` (root = block_1, the line-56 guard):

- block_1 (line 56 `sc != null`)
  - block_0 (exit/empty)
  - block_2 (line 58 init)
    - block_3 (line 60 null check)
      - block_4 (line 60 `size() > 0`)
        - block_5 (lines 62-64 promos + loop header setup)
  - block_6 (line 64 for-each)
    - block_7 (lines 66-68 loop body)
    - block_8 (line 72 shipping total)
      - block_9 (line 74 `cartItemTotal >= 25`)
        - block_10 (line 75 insurance)
  - block_11 (lines 81-83 shipping promos + cart total)

The idom data places block_6 directly under block_1 (idom=1) rather than under block_5; dominator frontiers are empty.

Which block guards the discount logic: block_4 (the `size() > 0` half of line 60) is the immediate dominator of the item-promotion/loop chain (5 → 6 → 7), so it gates `applyCartItemPromotions` and the per-item savings accumulation. Block_9 guards only the insurance add-on (line 75). Block_1 guards everything.

Caveat: block_6's stated idom of 1 contradicts the CFG, where 5 is its only predecessor — the tree appears conservative there.

events.text: This slice result looks wrong. Inspect the CFG/PDG and tell me whether the edge is real.

events.name: Bash

input.command: rgctl -f json inspect priceShoppingCart pdg --edge-layer data

events.text:
The slice output isn't a bug in the slicer — it faithfully reproduces the PDG: `inspect priceShoppingCart pdg --edge-layer data` contains exactly the same three edges node_7→node_8 (`sc`, `sci`, `getQuantity`). So the edge is real *in the model* but spurious *in the source*.

Why it's spurious:

- The `getQuantity` edge can't be def-use: line 66 only *reads* `sci.getQuantity()`; it never defines it. The same holds for `sci`.
- `sc` is a false dependence: line 66 writes field `cartItemPromoSavings`, while line 68 reads/writes `cartItemTotal` (`ShoppingCartService.java:66-68`). Different fields — no value flows.

This is a field-/alias-insensitive model: any mutation of the receiver object `sc` (or any statement mentioning a name) is treated as a definition that reaches later uses. That's also why the slice found no genuine loop-carried `68→68` dependence on `cartItemTotal`, nor the `58→68` init (`initShoppingCartForPricing` sets `cartItemTotal=0`, line 91).

Bottom line: the 66→68 edge is an object-level artifact, not a real data flow; treat the slice's "line 66 contributes to `sc` at 68" claim as unsound.
